candidates.notes: Lyricist death (1839), 1819 publication and hymn number 55 confirmed from fetched pages. The title is the first line, so the 5-word run is not verified and is only 4 words; alt_words must be set from verse 1 before use. Too easy as written.

candidates.notes: Franzén d. 14 Aug 1847 (sv.wikipedia), first published 1812 and listed as no. 53 in the 1819 Advent section (sv.wikisource). Title equals the first line, so the 5-word run is not verified and is only 4 words; alt_words must be set from verse 1 before use.

candidates.title: Gör porten hög, gör dörren bred
candidates.first_line: Gör porten hög, gör dörren bred
candidates.translator: Jakob Arrhenius; revised by Jesper Swedberg and Johan Olof Wallin
candidates.notes: Chain: Weissel (d. 1635 per de.wikipedia disambiguation page), Arrhenius translation 1694 (d. 13 Apr 1725), Swedberg revision (d. 1735), Wallin 1816 revision printed 1819 (d. 1839). Qualifies, but the title is 6 words and most of it is the first five words, so alt_words is required from verse 1. Verse text was not retrievable with the available tools.

candidates.title: Världens Frälsare kom här
candidates.notes: Olaus Petri translated it from Luther, first published 1536 in Swenske Songer (d. 19 Apr 1552). Wallin revised it (d. 1839). Title equals the first line and is only 4 words, so the 5-word run is not verified; alt_words must be set from verse 1 before use.

candidates.title: Av himlens höjd oss kommet är
candidates.first_line: Av himlens höjd oss kommet är
candidates.translator: Samuel Ödmann and Johan Olof Wallin (1817 reworking)
candidates.notes: Luther's Vom Himmel hoch, Swedish text by Olaus Martini (1557-1609), reworked by Ödmann (d. 2 Oct 1829) and Wallin (d. 1839) in 1817; 1695 psalmbok listing is the earliest date the page names. Title is 6 words, so the first 5 words are most of it; alt_words is required from verse 1. Verse text was not retrievable with the available tools.
